production.note: US model years. KBB's Purosangue listing is headed 2025 and links a '2024' model year; no earlier US model year is listed. Still on sale. Ferrari unveiled the car in September 2022 (ferrari-purosangue-release).

body.note: Ferrari: 'the first ever four-door, four-seater car in the Prancing Horse's 75-year history'. Ferrari avoids the word SUV, but under the data guide's vocabulary a high-riding four-door all-wheel-drive car is an SUV.

displacementL.note: 6,496 cc. Ferrari: 'Overall displacement 6496 cc'; Evo panel: 'V12, 6496cc' (evo-purosangue).

fuel.note: Footnote: 'with 98 RON petrol'. Top Gear: 'no hybrid assistance whatsoever' (topgear-purosangue).

drivetrain.note: Ferrari: 'The Power Transfer Unit (PTU) is coupled in front of the engine to provide a unique 4×4 transmission.' Automatically engaging front drive, so AWD under the guide.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 725 cv x 0.98632 = 715.1, rounded to 715 hp. Quote (Ferrari release as reproduced by the Ferrari Owners' Club, 'This article is from Ferrari Media'): "Max. power output* 725 cv at 7750 rpm", footnote 'with 98 RON petrol, including 5 cv of dynamic ram'. Evo's panel prints '715bhp @ 7750rpm' (evo-purosangue); KBB's US listing shows '715 hp' (kbb-purosangue). No separate SAE rating published by Ferrari for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: DRY weight: 2,033 kg x 2.20462 = 4,481.99, rounded to 4,482 lb. Quote (Ferrari release): "Dry weight** 2033 kg", footnote '**With optional lightweight content'. Evo's panel agrees and labels it dry: "Weight | 2033kg (dry) (357bhp/ton)", and its text says 'Bone dry and with lightweight options fitted, the Purosangue is 2033kg.' (evo-purosangue). No kerb weight was found: Ferrari's release gives none, Top Gear's review prints none and KBB's listing has none. Step 4 of the weight order (manufacturer dry weight), itself for a car with lightweight options, so a standard car in running order is considerably heavier.
